title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
coram: Ashok Bhushan, J. & R.A. Singh, J.
disposition: Writ petition allowed; the reduction of contracted load from 8 MVA to 1.25 MVA held to have stood approved on 19.4.2006, effective from 1.5.2006
headnote: A licensee's decision to reduce a consumer's contracted load, once taken, leaves only ministerial steps, and cannot be undone by later insistence on requirements not demanded at the time. The petitioner (a loss-making two-wheeler manufacturer, notified a 'Relief Undertaking' under the U.P. Industrial Undertaking (Special Provisions for Prevention of Unemployment) Act, 1966, and later a sick unit) applied on 31.3.2006 to reduce load from 8 MVA to 1.25 MVA after a lock-out halted production; the licensee agreed in a signed meeting on 19.4.2006, subject only to ministerial conditions, and the UPERC (8.5.2006) raised no objection. The Court held: (i) the reduction stood approved on 19.4.2006, effective from the first day of the following month (1.5.2006) under Clause 4.41(e); (ii) the relief-undertaking notification under ss.3-4 of the 1966 Act operates as a statutory stay of recovery, satisfying the 'stay by Court/Forum' condition of Clause 4.49; (iii) the unamended Clause 4.49 (which then accepted a bond or any instrument, including an affidavit of undertaking, not only a bank guarantee) governed the 31.3.2006 application, so the later demand for a bank guarantee (based on the 14.9.2006 amendment) was irrelevant; and (iv) no UPERC approval was needed for a licensee's load-reduction decision. Continuing to bill at 8 MVA after a production halt was unjust. This judgment was AFFIRMED by the Supreme Court in Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. v. LML Ltd., (2010) 6 SCC 165.

holding_units.topic: Load reduction stood approved on the licensee's decision; unamended Clause 4.49 governs and only ministerial steps remained
holding_units.question: Where the licensee decided to reduce load on a complete application, can it later refuse effect for want of a bank guarantee introduced by a subsequent amendment, and from when does the reduction take effect?
holding_units.holding: No. The load reduction stood approved by the licensee's signed decision of 19.4.2006, at which time no shortcoming in the application or non-compliance with Clauses 4.41/4.49 was pointed out; only ministerial steps remained. The application dated 31.3.2006 was governed by Clause 4.49 as it then stood, which accepted a bond or any instrument (the word 'instrument' being wide enough to include the affidavit of undertaking filed) and not only a bank guarantee; the requirement of a bank guarantee introduced by the 14.9.2006 amendment did not apply, so the later demands for a bank guarantee were of no consequence. No UPERC approval was required for a licensee's load-reduction decision. Under Clause 4.41(e) the reduction takes effect from the first day of the following month, i.e. 1.5.2006.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Lock-out from 7.3.2006 halted production; application of 31.3.2006 to reduce 8 MVA to 1.25 MVA; signed licensee decision on 19.4.2006 subject only to ministerial conditions; UPERC (8.5.2006) raised no objection; bank-guarantee demanded only later (4.10.2006 / 20.3.2007) on the amended Code.

holding_units.code: U.P. Industrial Undertaking (Special Provisions for Prevention of Unemployment) Act, 1966
holding_units.clause: ss.3-4 (relief-undertaking notification) r/w Clause 4.49, Supply Code 2005
holding_units.topic: A relief-undertaking notification operates as a statutory stay of recovery satisfying Clause 4.49
holding_units.question: Does a 'Relief Undertaking' notification under ss.3-4 of the 1966 Act satisfy Clause 4.49's condition of a stay of recovery 'by any Court/Forum/Tribunal/Commission' where there is no such stay order?
holding_units.holding: Yes. Under s.4 of the 1966 Act the liabilities of a notified relief undertaking accruing before the relevant date stand suspended while the notification is in force, and all proceedings for their enforcement are stayed. As the petitioner was a notified relief undertaking when it applied (31.3.2006), the recovery of arrears is to be treated as stayed, satisfying the 'stay' condition of Clause 4.49; the respondents' contention that Clause 4.49 was inapplicable for want of a court/forum stay was rejected. The declaration binds all instrumentalities of the State, including the licensee.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Relief-undertaking notification of 24.6.2004 under s.3(1) of the 1966 Act, extended to 23.6.2007, in force when the load-reduction application was made; subsequent BIFR/1985-Act proceedings post-dated the application and were not relied on.

principle_tags.application: A loss-making unit notified as a 'Relief Undertaking' cannot be burdened with billing at the pre-reduction load after production has halted; the relief declaration binds the licensee.

A load-reduction application is governed by the Code as it stood when the application was made (here the unamended Clause 4.49 accepting bond/instrument), not by a later amendment introducing a bank-guarantee requirement.
A notification under ss.3-4 of the 1966 Act suspends pre-notification liabilities and stays their enforcement, satisfying the stay condition of Clause 4.49.

lead_authorities.name: Modern Syntax (I) Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Tribunal, Jaipur

not_decided.point: The quantum of arrears and the consequences of the subsequent BIFR proceedings
not_decided.note: The arrears dispute abided separate settlement/BIFR proceedings; the BIFR orders post-dated the application and were not gone into.

authorities.name: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. v. LML Ltd.
authorities.proposition: Affirmed this judgment: the load reduction stood approved on the licensee's decision and the consumer was entitled to have its load treated as reduced.
authorities.how_treated: Subsequent history - this High Court judgment was affirmed by the Supreme Court (recorded in the corpus as SCJ-038).

authorities.name: Modern Syntax (I) Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Tribunal, Jaipur
authorities.proposition: The effect of a relief-undertaking notification is that any right, obligation or liability accrued before the undertaking was declared a relief undertaking, and any remedy for its enforcement, stands suspended, and all proceedings related thereto pending before any court/tribunal/authority are stayed during the currency of the notification.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on to hold that the relief-undertaking notification operated as a stay of recovery satisfying Clause 4.49.

authorities.name: K. Sambasivaraju v. M.V.S.R. Chandrayya Chetty
authorities.proposition: The word 'instrument' (as in s.2(14) of the Stamp Act, 1899) must receive an extensive meaning including an affidavit.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on to hold that the affidavit of undertaking qualified as an 'instrument' acceptable under the unamended Clause 4.49.
